narr: During the afternoon of Tuesday, July 5th, a complex of thunderstorms moved from South Dakota, eastward along a stationary front that lied near the Iowa border. North of this front, several lines of thunderstorms developed and moved eastward across far southern Minnesota. Although a few damage reports were noted, the main hazard was the increasing threat of heavy rainfall and flash flooding. Two areas of thunderstorms from southern Minnesota, and northern Iowa merged into a large complex as it slowly progressed to the east-southeast. Rainfall totals in a 3 hour period ranged from two to locally five inches from near Blue Earth in Faribault County, east to Albert Lea. The heaviest occurred over Albert Lea, and between Wells and Kiester in eastern Faribault County.
ev: Heavy rain caused flooding across much of western, southern, and central Freeborn County, with significant damage to numerous roads, bridges, and ditches in multiple townships, affecting areas in and near Shell Rock Watershed. Flooding caused major damage to two homes in Alden and two in Albert Lea, with walls collapsed. One more home in Albert Lea sustained minor damage. Local media also showed two vehicles fully submerged at the intersection of Franks Avenue and East 8th Street in Albert Lea. There were also cars submerged in a parking lot on Main Street and South Washington Avenue.
